title: security-eng-sync-notes-2026-03-06
content:
Security Engineering Sync - Notes (2026-03-06)

Attendees: Aisha Gupta (owner), Liam Chen, Morgan Reyes, Diego Alvarez, Priya Shah, Alice Ngo (observability), Tom Becker (SRE - partial)

Agenda:
- Quick round robin / blockers
- Vulnerability triage updates (dependabot, third-party libs)
- Secrets detection & remediation status
- Threat modeling follow-ups for Dedicated control plane change
- Action items and next steps

1) Round-robin / blockers
- Aisha: blocked briefly on vendor cert exchange for private deployments (legal review delay). Raised to legal; expect resolution by 3/10.
- Liam: finishing PoC for improved container runtime isolation; needs security review for syscall whitelist (RDW-2345).
- Morgan: working with infra on KV cache encryption benchmarks; deferred perf tests until quorum from SRE.

2) Vulnerability triage
- Summary since last sync: 6 new findings flagged by OSS-scan and Dependabot.
  - High: async-http-client CVE-2026-1001 -> affects internal ingestion service. Patch available (1.4.3). Assigned to Diego (JIRA: RDW-2345). Mitigation: upgrade + run smoke test on staging.
  - Medium: tjws TLS configuration warning in legacy test harness -> low exposure; scheduled for removal in next sprint. Owner: Morgan.
  - Low: dev-deps outdated in samples repo -> auto-upgrade via dependabot; monitoring.
- Decision: For all high/critical findings we apply patch to staging within 48 hours, run canary, then promote to prod within 7 days unless breaking tests. Documented process link: CONFLUENCE-SEC-PLAT-482.
- Action: Diego to submit PR for async-http-client upgrade and add integration smoke test (due 2026-03-08).
- Action: Aisha to trigger emergency CI windows with SRE for staging canary (coord with Tom).

3) Secrets detection & remediation
- New findings: GitGuardian alerted on 3 secrets in historical commits in private-deployments examples repo. Two were service account keys rotated previously (no active use), one is a leftover API key for a sandbox account.
  - Steps taken: keys revoked where applicable; secrets removed from git history using BFG and rewritten branches pushed. Team note: coordinate with consumers before force-pushing to shared branches.
- Gaps identified: internal dev onboarding docs still encourage legacy key creation flow. Need to update onboarding to emphasize short-lived creds / OIDC. Owner: Priya.
- Tooling: proposal to add pre-commit hook + CI check that fails PR if secret pattern matches baseline. Diego to prototype (RDW-2361).
- Action: Priya to update onboarding docs and open a PR for short-lived creds guide (due 2026-03-12).

4) Threat modeling - Dedicated control plane change (follow-up)
- Context: Product is moving to a consolidated control plane for Dedicated customers (RFC posted). Security concerns raised around tenant isolation boundary and cross-tenant telemetry.
- Notes from threat session:
  - Resurface attack surface: control plane API auth, telemetry collection pipeline, rollout canaries, and backup snapshot access.
  - Proposed mitigations: tenant-scoped encryption keys (KMS integration), strict RBAC for control plane operations, telemetry pseudonymization before cross-tenant aggregation, and separate backup buckets per tenant with customer-managed keys optional.
- Outstanding risks: Telemetry pseudonymization latency and impact on observability; backup access auditability when customers manage keys.
- Decision: Move forward with KMS per-tenant prototype and RBAC hardening for stage gating. Telemetry pseudonymization to be evaluated in a follow-up spike.
- Action: Morgan to lead KMS prototype (collab with platform-engineering). Spike due 2026-03-20.

5) Observability and alerts (brief)
- Alice noted an uptick in false-positive security alerts from new rule set; needs tuning. Aim: reduce noise by 30% before next release.
- Action: Alice + Diego to run alert tuning session (2026-03-09).

6) Incidents / post-mortems
- No new production security incidents since last sync.
- Post-mortem for 2026-02-25 (staging misconfiguration) draft is in Confluence and assigned to Tom for final edits. Link: CONFLUENCE-SEC-INC-2026-02-25.

7) Open discussion / questions
- Liam: syscall whitelist approach may break some ML inference optimized kernels; proposal to maintain a narrow allowlist per runtime flavor. Team agrees to a hybrid approach and to document runtime profiles.
- Priya: ask about rotating internal service tokens monthly vs quarterly. Consensus: move to 30-day rotation for high-privilege tokens, 90-day for low-scope tokens. Update secrets policy doc.

8) Action items (owner — due)
- Diego Alvarez — submit PR to upgrade async-http-client and add integration smoke test (RDW-2345) — due 2026-03-08.
- Aisha Gupta — coordinate emergency CI window with SRE for staging canary — due 2026-03-07.
- Priya Shah — update onboarding docs to deprecate legacy key creation; PR for short-lived creds guide — due 2026-03-12.
- Diego Alvarez + Alice Ngo — alert tuning session to reduce FP noise — scheduled 2026-03-09.
- Morgan Reyes — lead KMS per-tenant prototype spike (collab with platform-engineering) — due 2026-03-20.
- Liam Chen — draft runtime syscall profile doc and submit for review — due 2026-03-15.

Notes / Misc:
- Reminder: security-eng channel will host a mid-week async vuln update on Tuesday mornings. Post summary to #security-eng and tag on-call.
- Next sync: 2026-03-13 11:00 PT.

Unresolved / carryover items:
- Telemetry pseudonymization spike scheduling and perf impact measurement.
- Final decision on backup key management UX for Private customers.

End of notes.
